results.content:
### Is Slashy secure enough for a company?

It holds SOC 2 Type II and CASA Tier 2, encrypts at rest with AES-256, states that it does not train on customer data, and enforces zero data retention with its AI providers. The Enterprise tier adds SSO and SCIM.

### What is the closest alternative to Slashy?

For draft quality on Gmail, Fyxer is the nearest like-for-like. For the same assistant idea without the Gmail restriction and with a much wider integration surface, Carly is the closer match to what most Slashy evaluators are actually trying to buy.

## Ready to automate your busywork?

Carly schedules, researches, and briefs you—so you can focus on what matters.

See what people say [...] Best for: anyone who liked Slashy’s premise and is either on Outlook or needs the assistant to reach past email and calendar.

Driving it from your own code, provisioning agents per tenant, embedding it in your product, or running high volume is available. Book a call with the team and we will scope it to your setup.

## 2. Fyxer

The closest like-for-like on the drafting side, and the most common head-to-head. It writes replies in your voice, organizes the inbox, and takes meeting notes, with a similar “it learns how you write” pitch.

vs. Slashy: overlapping enough that the decision usually comes down to which one’s drafts sound more like you after a week. Worth trialing both on the same inbox rather than reading feature tables. Fyxer alternatives covers that field in more depth. [...] Best for: heavy email volume where draft quality is the whole decision.

## 3. Superhuman

A different theory of the problem. Superhuman’s answer is speed: keyboard-first, aggressively fast, with AI added on top of an email client rather than an assistant bolted onto Gmail. If your issue is that processing mail is slow rather than that you want someone else to do it, this is the honest fit.

vs. Slashy: Superhuman makes you faster at your inbox. Slashy tries to remove you from it. Those are opposite goals and people usually know which one they want.

Watch for: it is a client, so you are changing where you read mail, not adding a layer. Superhuman alternatives if that trade is the sticking point.

Best for: people who genuinely like doing email and want to do it in half the time.

results.content:
### Can AI task extraction tools work with on-premise email servers or only cloud-based services like Gmail and Outlook?

Most Slashy alternatives lean on cloud email, connecting to Gmail and Microsoft 365 through standard OAuth. On-premise Exchange servers usually need extra setup through Exchange Web Services (EWS) or a hybrid deployment, where some mailbox functionality still routes through Microsoft’s cloud. Tools that support MCP can give you more room to work with custom email infrastructure, though the implementation gets a lot more involved. If you have strict data residency requirements or air-gapped systems, check the integration architecture carefully before you commit to any platform. [...] The market offers 40+ Slashy alternatives in 2026. Which one fits comes down to what you actually need: calendar optimization, project management, or inbox-driven execution across several communication channels. [...] Slashy reaches beyond pure inbox management by offering access through iMessage and Slack on top of its core email features. Its design philosophy still treats email as the main workspace, though, rather than putting every channel on equal footing.

Multi-channel integration requires different architectural approaches:

 Native integration: Direct API connections to each platform for real-time monitoring
 Webhook-based: Triggered responses when activity occurs in connected tools
 Unified interface: Single view that aggregates messages from all sources
 Cross-channel context: Understanding that an email reply relates to a Slack conversation about the same project
